score_meanings.promise_vocabulary: 0 drifts into claims/profiles/central trust-ledger framing, 5 stays promise-first and pCID-specific
score_meanings.simplicity_durability: 0 overbuilt or fragile, 5 minimal, durable, and small-device-friendly under the 100-year goal

promise_theory_rules: A promise is a scoped declaration of intent.
No agent can make a promise on behalf of another agent.
Trust is a local assessment of whether a promise will be kept.
Promises to receive or use are not equivalent to obligations, impositions, or promises to give.
promise_theory_references: Mark Burgess, In Search of Certainty
Mark Burgess, Promise Theory: Principles and Applications

assessment.rationale: Strong fit as a Promise-Theory-first evidence layer for recording that Alice promised storage of C and that Bob later observed a successful serve. It is especially strong on auditability and promise vocabulary, though it is more an accounting/index pattern than a full storage interaction design, so failure handling and scenario completeness are only moderate.
strengths: Promise-first wording centered on who promised what and what was later observed.
Explicitly localizes trust and limits the artifact to descriptive evidence.
Durable citation/indexing structure is well matched to later audit of kept storage promises.
Clear boundary against authorization, certification, or dispute-settlement authority.
weaknesses: Does not by itself define the storage protocol details or retrieval evidence format for this scenario.
Failure and ambiguity handling are mentioned but not deeply worked through for storage-specific edge cases.
The pattern may need more explicit guidance on representing time-bounded retention promises.
risks: Could still drift back toward ledger-like or quasi-certification framing if implementations overstate what the index proves.
May underspecify the evidence needed to represent retention duration versus a single successful retrieval.
open_questions: How should an index entry bind chunk C, the storage-retention interval, and Bob's later successful retrieval evidence in a compact durable form?
What minimum evidence set distinguishes a kept storage promise from a one-off successful serve when retention duration matters?
assessment.authority_boundary: Evidence index only; it records promise evidence and local observations, but does not certify conformance, grant authorization, or settle disputes.

autonomous_agents.note: Promises and later observations are attributed to specific agents, preserving agent autonomy.

scoped_intent.note: Promises are scoped to pCID-referenced payloads or services and later observations about keep, break, refusal, or ambiguity.

no_promises_for_others.note: The design asks which agent promised what and avoids making promises on behalf of other agents.

no_guaranteed_outcomes.note: The index is descriptive evidence only and does not guarantee that promises were kept.

local_trust_assessment.note: The docs explicitly say trust remains a local judgment for Alice, Bob, or Carol.

accept_use_not_obligation.note: The design records evidence about promises and observations; it does not treat receipt or use as an obligation.
